M1.reason: Measured overlap clears 0.80 in every view (0.919, 0.852, 0.806), but the top view shows a real outline difference. The original's strap is an irregular, kinked loop hanging off the front-left and front-right. The reproduction's is a smooth symmetric V that reaches further out at the front-bottom. The reproduction's box is also more square in plan, while the original's corners are cut harder into a near-octagon. In the front and side views the reproduction's strap shows as a sloped wedge at the base, where the original's lies as a flat band.

M2.reason: 34.6 x 26.4 x 7.0 against 34.6 x 26.4 x 6.8. Every axis is within 10% (height is +3%).

M3.reason: It has the body, the strap and the device with screen and red/green lights, but two parts are wrong. On top, the original's device sits recessed in a cavity in the front half of the lid, with a grey mechanism visible inside it (front-left and front-right views). The reproduction has no recess: it puts a flat control strip on the top and moves the screen onto the sloped front chamfer. On the sides, the original has a large dark panel with two round knobs or speakers toward one end (left and right views). The reproduction has only a small black square and a round strap stud.

M4.reason: Measured mean deltaE is 17.7, over the line of 15, so 2 is not possible. The white body and red markings match. The strap is wrong: the original's is a mottled grey-brown, the reproduction's a clean khaki/tan (clearest in the front, left, right and angle views). The original's body is greyer and dirtier than the reproduction's bright white.

M5.reason: The red cross and the mirrored FIRST AID lettering on top are there and in place, as are the long red arrow markings down the side edges. But the reproduction adds red '+'/'x' marks on all four top corners and on the side chamfers, which the original does not have. It turns the original's arrow and small-print markings into plain red lines with dots, and it drops the grime and wear across the original's lid. The side device detail (knobs) is reduced to a black square.

M6.reason: At game size it reads as the same kind of object: a white first-aid case with a red cross and a strap. Side by side, though, a player would see that the original's dark recessed cavity on the lid is now a flat panel with a green screen on the front slope, that the strap is a different colour, and that the corners carry red marks the original lacks. They would not take it for the original.

M7.reason: The front is the same: the device and the strap loop face the front in the top and angle views. It is upright and lies flat on its base at the same height as the original.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes and the mesh looks closed, not inside out and not floating. But it has 712 triangles against the original's 99, more than seven times over and well past the limit of twice (198).
